body:
Context. claude.ai's connector dialog now offers 'Use Anthropic's hosted client metadata (Recommended)' - CIMD (the OAuth client-id-metadata-document draft). The client_id IS an https URL; the authorization server fetches the client's metadata (name, redirect_uris) from that URL and validates against it. No registration write. Today Loam supports only DCR, and one afternoon of connector testing left 13 dead connector-NNNN clients in the grant ledger. CIMD ends the accumulation and matches the dialog's recommended path.

Build.
- /oauth/authorize and /oauth/token accept a client_id that is an https URL. Fetch the metadata document; validate the requested redirect_uri by EXACT string match against the document's redirect_uris. PKCE S256 stays mandatory. token_endpoint_auth stays 'none'. Verify field names against the current draft during build and record the draft version in the working notes.
- Advertise client_id_metadata_document_supported: true in /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
- Identity and grants: the client_id URL is the client's identity in the grant ledger. loam grant <client_id_url> --verb=register --prefix=<ns>: must accept a URL id as an opaque string - no canonicalization beyond the draft's requirements.
- THE FETCH IS A SERVER-SIDE REQUEST TO AN ATTACKER-INFLUENCED URL. Every fence below is mandatory, and each earns its own red rail:
  (1) https only; refuse userinfo@ in the URL.
  (2) Refuse IP-literal hosts, localhost, .local/.internal names, and any resolved address in loopback, RFC1918, link-local, or unique-local ranges - check the CONNECTED address, not just the name (DNS rebinding).
  (3) Refuse redirects outright (simpler than re-fencing each hop).
  (4) Response cap 64KB; timeout 5s; content-type must be application/json.
  (5) The fetched client_name is untrusted display text: pass it through plainText (T172) before the consent page, terminal, or log renders it.
- Cache the document by exact URL with a short TTL (about 5 minutes) so an authorize burst costs one fetch (H8). Never cache a failure.

Acceptance criteria - every rail two-sided, both levels:
(a) A CIMD authorize+token round-trip succeeds against a local fixture metadata server; a mismatched redirect_uri refuses. Verify: new test/server/oauth-cimd.test.ts.
(b) Each SSRF fence refuses its case (http URL, IP literal, localhost, redirect, oversized body, wrong content-type) AND the legitimate fixture URL still passes beside it. Verify: same file.
(c) DCR is UNCHANGED: the existing connector flow still round-trips (the bystander side). Verify: same file, driving the existing register+token path.
(d) The AS metadata advertises the support flag. Verify: same file.
(e) The consent surface renders a hostile client_name scrubbed (control chars, bidi). Verify: same file.

Merge tier: WIDENED DOOR - the store now trusts a fetched document where it used to require a registration write. Myk merges the PR, per merge-by-risk. One-line for the PR: a client never registered here can now authorize, if its https metadata document vouches for its redirect.
title: The OAuth door reads a client-id metadata document — CIMD, no registration write
